name: Question 19
problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13957423/assets/7f1573d17cb9a603727b644da6598355875b0be4b8c43a382e562155cb7a095c.png)

The line segment $\overset{―}{XY}$ is a diameter of a circle. Given that $X$ and $Y$ have coordinates $(-1,-3)$ and $(3,1)$, respectively, what is the equation of the circle?
worked_solution:
The general equation of a circle with radius $r$ centered at the point $(a,b)$ is

$$
(x-a)^{2}+(y-b)^{2}={r}^{2}.
$$

Using the distance formula to compute the distance between the points $X(-1,-3)$ and $Y(3,1),$ we find that the length of the diameter is 

$$
\begin{aligned}XY & =\sqrt{(-1-3)^{2}+(-3-1)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(-4)^{2}+(-4)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{16+16} \\  & =\sqrt{16\cdot 2} \\  & =4\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

So the radius of the circle is 

$$
r=\frac{4\sqrt{2}}{2}=2\sqrt{2}.
$$

Since the center of a circle is the midpoint of the diameter, to find the center we use the midpoint formula as follows:

$$
(\frac{{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}}{2},\frac{{y}_{1}+{y}_{2}}{2})=(\frac{-1+3}{2},\frac{-3+1}{2})=(1,-1)
$$

So our circle has radius $r=2\sqrt{2}$ and center $(a,b)=(1,-1),$ and therefore it is represented by the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-a)^{2}+(y-b)^{2} & ={r}^{2} \\ (x-1)^{2}+(y-(-1))^{2} & ={(2\sqrt{2})}^{2} \\ (x-1)^{2}+(y+1)^{2} & =8\end{aligned}
$$

Question 19

The line segment XY― is a diameter of a circle. Given that X and Y have coordinates (−1,−3) and (3,1), respectively, what is the equation of the circle?

a
 (x−1)2+(y−1)2=8
b
 (x−1)2+(y+1)2=32
c
 (x+1)2+(y−1)2=8
d
(x−1)2+(y+1)2=8
e
 (x+1)2+(y−1)2=32
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The general equation of a circle with radius r centered at the point (a,b) is
(x−a)2+(y−b)2=r2.

Using the distance formula to compute the distance between the points X(−1,−3) and Y(3,1), we find that the length of the diameter is

XY=(−1−3)2+(−3−1)2=(−4)2+(−4)2=16+16=16⋅2=42.

So the radius of the circle is r=422=22.

Since the center of a circle is the midpoint of the diameter, to find the center we use the midpoint formula as follows: (x1+x22,y1+y22)=(−1+32,−3+12)=(1,−1)

So our circle has radius r=22 and center (a,b)=(1,−1), and therefore it is represented by the following equation: (x−a)2+(y−b)2=r2(x−1)2+(y−(−1))2=(22)2(x−1)2+(y+1)2=8
